actions: Ran a reduced source-derived causal control to test whether Oja tracking itself is uniquely responsible for performance under low-rank representational drift. This is not an exact SPLiT reproduction and intentionally omits the paper's recurrent teacher-feedback term.

Synthetic setup: ambient activity dimension 24, latent manifold dimension 3, 1,600 online steps, drifting orthonormal latent basis, Gaussian latent states, small observation noise, scalar target linear in latent coordinates, normalized-LMS decoder updates. Compared (a) Oja-tracked latent basis + NLMS, (b) generic exponentially weighted covariance PCA with Procrustes alignment between successive bases + NLMS, (c) oracle current manifold + NLMS, (d) frozen initial manifold + NLMS, and (e) full-space NLMS.

Hyperparameters for Oja and generic PCA were selected on separate development seeds for each drift regime, then evaluated on 20 held-out paired seeds. Three drift rates were tested: slow 0.004, medium 0.018, fast 0.045 per synthetic rotation step; observation noise SD 0.03.

Held-out mean MSE: slow drift Oja 0.01149 vs generic aligned EW-PCA 0.00535 vs full-space NLMS 0.00536; medium drift Oja 0.08146 vs PCA 0.05481 vs full 0.05539; fast drift Oja 0.19465 vs PCA 0.15750 vs full 0.15827. Oracle current-manifold NLMS remained much lower, as expected, while frozen initial coordinates became especially poor at fast drift.

Paired bootstrap on Oja-minus-PCA MSE across 20 held-out seeds: slow +0.00615 with 95% CI approximately [-0.00000,+0.01422] (not resolved); medium +0.02664 [0.01207,0.04423]; fast +0.03714 [0.01951,0.05808]. Thus generic aligned EW-PCA significantly outperformed the tuned Oja tracker in the medium and fast reduced regimes. Oja nevertheless significantly outperformed the frozen initial subspace at fast drift: Oja-minus-static -0.09479, 95% CI [-0.16479,-0.03563].

This reduced control strengthens a narrower interpretation of SPLiT: adaptive subspace tracking can be valuable when the activity manifold moves, but the paper's current evidence plus this source-derived test do not establish that Oja tracking is uniquely superior to generic online subspace tracking or even well-conditioned full-space adaptation outside the paper's specific constrained RNN/feedback regime. The exact paper implementation and teacher-feedback coupling remain decisive missing pieces.

reduced_causal_control.development_tuning: separate development seeds per drift regime for Oja eta and EW-PCA beta/eigendecomposition interval
scope: No recurrent teacher-feedback term, autonomous replay, MNIST/Lorenz/Rossler dynamics, or exact paper hyperparameters are included.
The generic PCA tracker uses a global covariance eigendecomposition and Procrustes alignment, so it is a computational mechanism control rather than a biological-locality control.
Full-space NLMS is not FORCE/RLS and therefore does not reproduce the paper's full-space baseline failure mode.
Do not generalize these synthetic results to the published SPLiT tasks; use them only to prioritize matched low-rank baseline tests.

candidate_update.new_interpretation: Adaptive manifold tracking is plausibly useful under representational drift, but current evidence does not isolate Oja/SPLiT from generic online subspace conditioning. In a reduced held-out synthetic test, tuned aligned EW-PCA beat tuned Oja at medium/fast drift while Oja beat a frozen subspace at fast drift.
scope: Exact source reproduction remains required before changing the strength of the published claim.
The paper's teacher-feedback coupling could alter the comparison materially.
The next matched test should grant all methods the same low-dimensional coordinate budget and compare biological locality separately from computational performance.
